Fix a failure in CI

The ecosystem test for `eslint-plugin-unicorn` started failing after `core-js-compat` v3.50.0 was released on 2026-08-05. That version empties the support data for `es.promise.try` and `esnext.promise.try`. In 3.49.0 both held a full engine map, `"node": "23.0"` among them. In 3.50.0 both are `{}`. So `require("core-js/stable/promise")` now counts as still needed on any target, and the `no-unnecessary-polyfills` test that expects one error gets none.

The change is deliberate upstream. The core-js 3.50.0 changelog marks `Promise.try` as not properly supported in any engine, following [tc39/ecma262#3883](https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/pull/3883), so a patch release will not bring the old data back.

An example run in CI is https://github.com/eslint/eslint/actions/runs/31060131270/job/94013612129.

#### What changes did you make? (Give an overview)

Pinned `core-js-compat` to 3.49.0 in the plugin data, alongside the existing `eslint-plugin-eslint-plugin` pin. This is the same approach #21156 took for that pin.

#### Is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on?

`eslint-plugin-unicorn` depends on `core-js-compat` with a `^3.49.0` range, so moving the commit pin forward doesn't avoid this. 3.49.0 is the only published version that satisfies that range and still predates the change, so there is no newer pin to pick.

The plugin's own test needs an update before the pin can be dropped. That is tracked in sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn#3606.

Fixes #21190

Bumps [github/codeql-action](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) from 4 to 4.37.3.
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action's releases.

v4.37.3

No user facing changes.

v4.37.2

  • The new address format for the config-file input that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 is now enabled by default. In addition to the format described there, the remote= prefix can now be used to explicitly indicate that the input refers to a remote file. All previous input formats continue to be accepted as well. #4023
  • The CodeQL Action can now make use of configured private registries in Default Setup to retrieve CodeQL configuration files from remote repositories that require authentication. This will allow customers to store their CodeQL configuration in a single repository that can then be referenced by Default Setup workflows in other repositories. We expect to roll this and other, related changes out to everyone in July. #4007

v4.37.1

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.1. #4019

v4.37.0

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

v4.36.3

No user facing changes.

v4.36.2

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

v4.36.1

No user facing changes.

v4.36.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

v4.35.5

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

v4.35.4

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

v4.35.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.19.3 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 9 April 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.15, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3837
  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.3. #3865

v4.35.2

  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable is deprecated and will be removed in May 2026. If you are affected by this, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #3795
  • The Git version 2.36.0 requirement for improved incremental analysis now only applies to repositories that contain submodules. #3789

# Language plugins: invalid `language` id error doesn't enumerate the registered language keys

## What problem does this feature solve?

When a flat-config object references a plugin's `languages` namespace with a `language` key
that doesn't exist on that plugin (a typo, e.g. `language: "sh/shell"` instead of the
registered `language: "sh/sh"`), `Config`'s constructor throws:

```
TypeError: Key "language": Could not find "shell" in plugin "sh".
```

(`lib/config/config.js`, `Config` constructor — the check right after `splitPluginIdentifier`.)

This message names the offending key but never lists what *would* have worked — the plugin
object's own `languages` keys are already in hand at the point the error is thrown
(`plugins[languagePluginName].languages`), but they're not surfaced. A user (or an author
following a plugin's own docs) has to go read the plugin's source/docs to locate the correct
`language` id instead of getting it from the error itself.

Reproduction (`eslint` 10.7.0, a real language-plugin package registering `languages: { sh:
ShellLanguage }`):

```js
import { Linter } from 'eslint';
import sh from '@eslint-sh/eslint-plugin';

new Linter().verify('echo hi\n', [
  { files: ['**/*.sh'], plugins: { sh }, language: 'sh/nope' },
], 'a.sh');
// TypeError: Key "language": Could not find "nope" in plugin "sh".
```

## What did you expect to happen?

Something closer to how the sibling `Key "languageOptions": Unexpected key "..." found.`
validation error behaves elsewhere in the same file (and how enum-style option errors read
throughout the codebase): name the value that was actually available. For example:

```
TypeError: Key "language": Could not find "nope" in plugin "sh". Available languages in
plugin "sh": "sh".
```

## What did you see instead?

```
TypeError: Key "language": Could not find "nope" in plugin "sh".
```

No enumeration of the plugin's actually-registered `languages` keys.

## Are you willing to submit a pull request to fix this?

Possibly — happy to discuss the exact message wording first.

---
We hit this in a DX study for a shell-script language plugin
(https://github.com/mike-north/eslint-sh) — filing this as a companion to #21170 (the related
"config references a plugin's language but omits `language`" diagnostic gap), since both
originate in the same `Config` constructor validation and share the same fix motivation: make
config-time language-selection mistakes self-diagnosing from the error message alone.

# Language-plugin RFC

## What problem does this feature solve?

A flat-config object that references a language-owning plugin (`plugins: { sh }`, where
`sh.languages.sh` exists) but forgets the `language: "sh/sh"` selector key produces two
confusing outcomes, neither of which names the actual mistake:

1. **Silent fallback, misleading error.** ESLint falls back to the default `"@/js"`
   language and tries to parse the non-JS file as JavaScript. For most non-JS source this
   throws a `Parsing error: Unexpected token ...` fatal lint message that never mentions
   `language`, the offending plugin, or that a language even exists to select.
2. **Hard crash pre-parse.** If the config object also sets `languageOptions` using keys
   that belong to the plugin's language (e.g. `languageOptions: { dialect: 'bash' }`),
   `Config`'s constructor (`lib/config/config.js`) validates those options against the
   **default JS language's** own schema before any plugin code ever runs, and throws
   `TypeError: Key "languageOptions": Unexpected key "dialect" found.` This throw happens
   synchronously inside `FlatConfigArray#getConfig` → `Config`'s constructor, is never
   caught by `Linter#verify`, `ESLint#lintFiles`, or any of the `eslint` CLI's own code, and
   propagates all the way to the CLI's top-level `main().catch(onFatalError)` — producing
   the generic "Oops! Something went wrong!" crash banner (`bin/eslint.js`) instead of a
   normal per-file lint message.

We hit this repeatedly in a DX study for a shell-script language plugin
(`@eslint-sh/eslint-plugin` / `sh-ast`): omitting `language: 'sh/sh'` was the single worst
first-run failure mode, and nothing in either error names the missing key. Investigation
(https://github.com/mike-north/eslint-sh/issues/63) confirmed **this is not something a
language plugin can detect or improve itself** — in both failure modes, ESLint's own core
code (the default JS `Language`'s `parse()`, or `Config`'s own `languageOptions` validation
against the default JS language) runs and either fails or throws *before* any plugin-owned
code path (`Language.parse`, `Language.validateLanguageOptions`, a rule's `create()`) is
ever reached. There is no `Language`/`Plugin` lifecycle hook that fires while a config
object referencing a plugin is being resolved but that plugin's language hasn't been
selected.

## What did you expect to happen?

At minimum, some actionable diagnostic naming the missing `language` key and candidate
plugin language ids, produced by ESLint core (since plugins cannot reach this codepath
themselves).

## What actually happened?

See the two failure modes above. Neither error mentions `language`, the plugin, or the
fact that a custom language exists and wasn't selected.

## Repro

```js
// eslint.config.mjs — using any language-owning plugin, e.g. our sh plugin:
import sh from 'eslint-sh';
export default [
  // missing `language: 'sh/sh'`
  { files: ['**/*.sh'], plugins: { sh }, languageOptions: { dialect: 'bash' } },
];
```

```
TypeError: Key "languageOptions": Unexpected key "dialect" found.
    at new Config (.../eslint/lib/config/config.js:506:10)
    at [finalizeConfig] (.../eslint/lib/config/flat-config-array.js:212:10)
    at FlatConfigArray.getConfigWithStatus (.../@eslint/config-array/dist/cjs/index.cjs:1411:55)
    at FlatConfigArray.getConfig (.../@eslint/config-array/dist/cjs/index.cjs:1429:15)
    at Linter._verifyWithFlatConfigArray (.../eslint/lib/linter/linter.js:1378:30)
```

Uncaught by every layer above it, so it surfaces via the CLI's top-level
`main().catch(onFatalError)` (`bin/eslint.js`) as the generic crash banner rather than a
normal lint result.

## Proposal (concrete, implementable without a new plugin hook)

Both changes are contained to `Config`'s constructor in `lib/config/config.js`, which
already has `plugins` and the resolved `languageOptions` in scope:

1. **Name the missing key's owner in the existing crash.** When the default JS language's
   `validateLanguageOptions` throws `Unexpected key "<key>"`, before rethrowing, probe the
   `plugins` map: for every plugin exposing a `languages` map, check whether that
   language's own `validateLanguageOptions(languageOptions)` accepts the same options
   object without throwing. If exactly one candidate accepts it, append a hint to the
   thrown `TypeError`'s message, e.g. `... Unexpected key "dialect" found. (Plugin "sh"
   defines a language "sh/sh" that accepts this option — did you forget \`language:
   "sh/sh"\` in this config object?)`.
2. **Warn on silent fallback.** When a config object sets `plugins` whose value(s) expose a
   non-empty `languages` map, but the object itself does not set an explicit `language` key
   (so the default `"@/js"` language is used), emit a config-time warning (or a low-severity
   lint message, consistent with how ESLint reports other config-shape issues) naming the
   available plugin language ids, e.g. `Config object matching these files declares
   plugin(s) with custom languages ('sh/sh') but does not select one via \`language\`;
   falling back to the default JavaScript language.`

Both are additive, backward compatible (no schema/behavior change for configs that already
work), and don't require inventing a new `Language`/`Plugin` lifecycle hook — they only use
information `Config` already has when constructing itself.

Install scripts still run in this phase, but a warning is shown after `npm install` when a package has an install script that isn't covered by `allowScripts`. Starting with npm 12, unapproved install scripts will no longer run by default ([official announcement](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-08-npm-install-time-security-and-gat-bypass2fa-deprecation/)).

On a fresh install with npm 11.16.0, the following warning appears:

```
npm warn allow-scripts 4 packages have install scripts not yet covered by allowScripts:
npm warn allow-scripts   core-js@3.49.0 (postinstall: node -e "try{require('./postinstall')}catch(e){}")
npm warn allow-scripts   cypress@14.5.4 (postinstall: node index.js --exec install)

npm warn allow-scripts   re2@1.25.2 (install: install-from-cache --artifact build/Release/re2.node ... || node-gyp -j max rebuild)
```

- `npm test` passes.
- `npx prettier --check package.json` passes.

## Summary

The `getter-return` rule reports false positives in two cases ([#21157](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/21157)):

1. **Wrong argument index** — a `get` method in the target object (3rd arg) is treated as a property descriptor:
   ```js
   Object.defineProperty({ get(key) {} }, "name", { value: 1 });
   ```
2. **Shadowed `Object`** — when `Object` is a local variable, the rule still treats `Object.defineProperty(...)` as a global call:
   ```js
   function f(Object) { Object.defineProperty({}, "k", { get() {} }); }
   ```

The root cause is that `getter-return` did its own manual AST traversal to detect `Object.defineProperty()`, but unlike the equivalent check in `no-setter-return`, it did not verify the argument position or that `Object` actually refers to the global.

## Changes

- **`lib/rules/utils/ast-utils.js`** — export two helpers already used by `no-setter-return`:
  - `isArgumentOfGlobalMethodCall(node, globalMethodName, argumentIndex)` — checks that `node` is the Nth argument of a call like `Object.defineProperty(...)`, and that the call is to the global (not a shadowed variable).
  - `isPropertyDescriptor(node)` — shorthand for `isArgumentOfGlobalMethodCall(node, "defineProperty", 2) || ...`

- **`lib/rules/getter-return.js`** — replace the inline `isPropertyDescriptor` / `isObjectDefinePropertyCall` / `isPropertyAccessOfObjectDefineProperties` helpers with the shared `isPropertyDescriptor` from `ast-utils`. This adds the missing argument-position and global-reference checks.

- **`lib/rules/no-setter-return.js`** / **`lib/rules/accessor-pairs.js`** — replace their local copies of `isArgumentOfGlobalMethodCall` / `isPropertyDescriptor` with the shared versions to avoid duplication.

- **`tests/lib/rules/getter-return.js`** — 6 new valid test cases covering both false-positive scenarios.

## Test results

All 542 tests across `getter-return` (76), `no-setter-return` (164), and `accessor-pairs` (302) pass.
title: fix(getter-return): avoid false positives with shadowed Object

### Environment

Node version: v24.15.0
npm version:  11.12.1
Local ESLint version: v10.4.0
Global ESLint version: 
Operating System: Windows 11 (NT 10.0.26200)


### What parser are you using?

Default (Espree)

### What did you do?

I ran the `no-unused-vars` rule on some code where I had an unused function declaration. When I used my editor's quick-fix to apply the `removeVar` suggestion on that function,it produced syntactically invalid JavaScript because it didn't account for ASI (Automatic Semicolon Insertion). 

Here's the minimal setup to see it happen:

<details>
<summary>Configuration</summary>

```js
{
  rules: { "no-unused-vars": "error" }
}

```


</details>

```js
const x = 1
function unused() {}
(a) => {}
```


### What did you expect to happen?

The `removeVar` suggestion should either produce syntactically valid JavaScript, or not be offered when removing the declaration would create an ASI hazard.


### What actually happened?

Applying the `removeVar` suggestion produced syntactically invalid JavaScript:

```js
const x = 1

(a) => {}
```

Without a semicolon after `const x = 1`, the parser interprets `1(a)` as a call expression on the numeric literal `1`, then hits `=>` and fails:

```
Unexpected token =>
```

The issue appears to originate from the FunctionDeclaration and ClassDeclaration removal paths in handleFixes, which call fixer.removeRange(parent.range) directly and do not appear to perform the ASI-safety checks used for VariableDeclarator removals

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://eslint.org/play/#eyJ0ZXh0IjoiY29uc3QgeCA9IDFcbmZ1bmN0aW9uIHVudXNlZCgpIHt9XG4oYSkgPT4ge31cbiIsIm9wdGlvbnMiOnsicnVsZXMiOnsibm8tdW51c2VkLXZhcnMiOlsiZXJyb3IiXX0sImxhbmd1YWdlT3B0aW9ucyI6eyJwYXJzZXJPcHRpb25zIjp7ImVjbWFGZWF0dXJlcyI6e319fX19

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.

### AI acknowledgment

- [ ] I did not use AI to generate this issue report.
- [x] (If the above is not checked) I have reviewed the AI-generated content before submitting.

### Additional comments

Also affects `ClassDeclaration`:

```js
const x = 1
class Unused {}
(a) => {}
```

Applying the `removeVar` suggestion produces the same invalid output and parser error.

For comparison, in an ASI-sensitive variable-declaration scenario, ESLint still reports the unused variable but suppresses the removal suggestion. This suggests that variable removals already have protection against unsafe declaration removal, while function and class removals do not.

To reproduce the issue, apply the removeVar suggestion for unused.

### ESLint version

v9.39.4

### What problem do you want to solve?

ESLint 9.39.4 (the current 9.x maintenance release) crashes during config loading in environments where the CommonJS `require` function exists but does not expose a `cache` object, for example Yarn Berry Plug'n'Play with the ESM loader enabled (`pnpEnableEsmLoader: true`) on recent Node.js 22.23.x/24.15.x releases.

The crash happens in `lib/config/config-loader.js`:

```
TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
    at loadConfigFile (.../eslint/lib/config/config-loader.js:234:24)
    at async ConfigLoader.calculateConfigArray (.../eslint/lib/config/config-loader.js:589:23)
```

caused by:
```js
delete require.cache[filePath];
```
throwing when `require.cache` is `undefined`.

This exact bug was already reported and fixed in #20813 / #20812, and both the original issue and the fix PR explicitly note it should be backported to v9 ("This affects ESLint 9.x as well... should be considered for backport to v9" / "This should be backported to v9 because the crash affects ESLint 9.x users in loader environments where `require.cache` is unavailable."). The fix was released in 10.3.0, but no 9.x patch release has followed.

Many projects (including ours) still pin ESLint ^9.39.x via shared config packages and cannot yet move to ESLint 10.x, so we're currently stuck pinning Yarn itself to an older release (4.15.0) as a workaround, purely to avoid hitting this ESLint bug.

### What do you think is the correct solution?

Cherry-pick the fix from #20812 onto the 9.x maintenance branch and release it as a new ESLint 9.x patch version (e.g. 9.39.5), applying the same guard:

```js
delete require.cache?.[filePath];
```

This is a minimal, backwards-compatible change (optional chaining on a cache-clearing side effect) with no behavioral impact when `require.cache` exists, and it unblocks projects on the 9.x line from the Yarn PnP + Node 22.23.x/24.15.x crash without needing to migrate to ESLint 10.x first.

[ ] Add something to the core
[ ] Other, please explain:

#### Why is this change needed?

Fixes #20014.

`no-use-before-define` currently treats all references inside a function expression in a variable initializer as deferred. That is correct for cases such as `const value = () => value`, because the function body cannot run until after the initializer completes.

The same assumption is too optimistic when the function expression is part of an initializer call, constructor call, tag call, or IIFE. In those cases, the initializer can run the function before the variable binding has been initialized, which creates the TDZ failure described in the issue.

Reporting these cases by default would change existing rule behavior, so this keeps the current default and adds `allowDeferredReferences`. Users can set it to `false` when they want the rule to treat initializer callbacks pessimistically.

The check is intentionally limited to places where initializer evaluation can immediately hand off or call the function expression. Direct function assignments, arrays or objects stored as values, and nested returned functions remain allowed because those references are still deferred by construction.

#### What would you like reviewers to focus on?

Please focus on whether the option boundary is narrow enough: it catches callbacks/IIFEs that can run during initialization while preserving the existing optimistic default and avoiding definitely deferred patterns.

Coming over from #19369: multiple users report seeing deprecation warnings from the `punycode` module. I.e.:

```plaintext
yarn eslint .
(node:13937) [DEP0040] DeprecationWarning: The `punycode` module is deprecated. Please use a userland alternative instead.
(Use `node --trace-deprecation ...` to show where the warning was created)
...
```

I investigated this in https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/19369#issuecomment-2614122158. Copying here: 

* I think the deprecation warning is actually from Yarn v1 and is **not ESLint or any of ESLint's dependencies**.
* The deprecation is from Yarn v1 calling to the _[built-in deprecated Node.js_ `punycode`](https://nodejs.org/api/punycode.html)_, not the _[npm `punycode` package](https://npmjs.com/package/punycode)_

In a fresh directory, running `npm init --yes; npm i eslint` for me gives:

```plaintext
added 85 packages, and audited 86 packages in 3s

22 packages are looking for funding
  run `npm fund` for details
```

Similar with `pnpm i eslint`.

However, with specifically `yarn add eslint`:

```plaintext
yarn add v1.22.19
info No lockfile found.
[1/4] 🔍  Resolving packages...
⠁ (node:13937) [DEP0040] DeprecationWarning: The `punycode` module is deprecated. Please use a userland alternative instead.
(Use `node --trace-deprecation ...` to show where the warning was created)
[2/4] 🚚  Fetching packages...
[3/4] 🔗  Linking dependencies...
[4/4] 🔨  Building fresh packages...
success Saved lockfile.
success Saved 74 new dependencies.
info Direct dependencies
└─ eslint@9.19.0
info All dependencies
├─ @eslint-community/eslint-utils@4.4.1
├─ ... (omitted from comment for brevity, see <details>)
✨  Done in 1.26s.
```

Re-running with `NODE_OPTIONS='--trace-deprecation' yarn add eslint`:

```plaintext
[1/4] 🔍  Resolving packages...
⠁ (node:14240) [DEP0040] DeprecationWarning: The `punycode` module is deprecated. Please use a userland alternative instead.
    at node:punycode:3:9
    at BuiltinModule.compileForInternalLoader (node:internal/bootstrap/realm:399:7)
    at BuiltinModule.compileForPublicLoader (node:internal/bootstrap/realm:338:10)
    at loadBuiltinModule (node:internal/modules/helpers:96:7)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1070:17)
    at TracingChannel.traceSync (node:diagnostics_channel:315:14)
    at wrapModuleLoad (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:215:24)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1304:12)
    at require (/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/yarn/lib/v8-compile-cache.js:159:20)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/yarn/lib/cli.js:56533:18)
[2/4] 🚚  Fetching packages...
```

So, I believe the usage of the _built-in Node.js_ `punycode` module comes from within Yarn v1.

I filed this issue to separate out the _"why am I getting deprecation warnings?"_ discussion out from the _"should ESLint fork AJV?"_ discussion. I think this is reasonable because the deprecation warnings are not from ESLint or AJV, and so shouldn't impact the forking discussion IMO.

Assuming the investigation didn't miss anything, I think we should close this as wontfix, right? Letting this issue just serve as a search result for when Yarn v1 users search the deprecation?
title: Bug: Deprecation warnings from punycode module
